Exact first-mean identity is exp(hC)exp(h(K-C))=exp(hM). Q=exp(-hC)exp(hM) is positive-spectrum upper triangular. A Metzler logarithm H=K-C with exp(hH)=Q cannot have below-diagonal positive entries (nonnegative power-series argument); its upper entries are uniquely determined by divided differences. The resolvent formula for (log Q)_13 has sign sign(sqrt(d1 d3)-d2), where d_i=exp(-hc_i), via reciprocal substitution and strict J monotonicity, equivalent to 2c2>=c1+c3. Both nearest couplings strictly positive; in 2x2 the sole logarithmic divided difference is positive. h>0 exact, including equal variances, noncommuting original matrices. Independent SciPy logm/expm checked 21 parameter-step settings, sign and exact moments; examples with (1,0,1) give K13<0. Numerical checks are secondary to integral proof.
